speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is going to be a long Budget Speech as there are many important things to cover.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I had one file and it took me one and a half hours.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I promise I will call for a recess in the middle.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Riding on the global upturn, Singapore’s economy picked up last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This exceeded the Government's forecast of 1% to 3% at the start of 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The good productivity growth has enabled firms to pay higher wages while staying competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The positive near-term outlook shows that the hard work of employers, workers and the Government is paying off.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The remaining two will be launched by the end of March.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The tripartite Future Economy Council (FEC) is now overseeing the implementation of these ITMs and the strategies laid out by the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Though new, the ITMs are helping to prepare our companies for a new phase of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, as part of the Precision Engineering ITM, several companies in the sector, like Univac Precision Engineering and Globaltronic Precision, have undertaken projects to make better use of digital technologies in their manufacturing processes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has enabled them to stay competitive and take advantage of the global economic recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We recognise, however, that some sectors, such as construction and marine and offshore engineering, continue to face headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we address such near-term concerns, the Budget must be a strategic and integrated plan to position Singapore for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Strategic because it should identify future needs and issues and propose early preparations to meet them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And integrated because it should pool together resources and integrate efforts across all stakeholders – workers, businesses, voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), the Government and our citizens – to build a better Singapore for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must prepare for three major shifts in the coming decade.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, is the shift in global economic weight towards Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be accompanied by broader shifts in the global order.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In recent years, several advanced economies have turned their attention inward in reaction to domestic pressures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Brexit has put a cloud of uncertainty over the United Kingdom (UK) and its trade with the European Union (EU) and the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And the United States' (US') recent tax changes and review of trade pacts will intensify competition and economic nationalism, fuelling anxieties worldwide.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Meanwhile, Asia will play a larger role in global trade and investment flows.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: China has set up a regional infrastructure bank and laid out bold plans under the Belt and Road initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: India is reforming its economy, easing restrictions on foreign investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Closer to home, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries are moving up the value chain and their middle-class population is growing rapidly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these developments represent significant opportunities for our firms and people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our economy must be geared to ride on and contribute to Asia’s growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, there are also potential threats to the stability and growth of our region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Tensions on the Korean peninsula and in the South China Sea can dampen investor confidence, while the threat of terrorism across the region remains very real.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second shift is the emergence of new technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Robotics and digital technologies are changing the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have already enabled the shift to Industry 4.0 and the rapid rise of e-commerce and a sharing economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are interacting with traditional businesses in different ways, sometimes as competing substitutes, sometimes as complementary enablers4.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New technologies are reshaping the economy and jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms will compete increasingly not on physical assets, but on intangible assets, such as intellectual property (IP), data and user networks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First-mover advantage and time to market will be key.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Securing better jobs and higher wages will not be just about how well we did in school, but how well we continue to learn, relearn, adapt and grow throughout our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are well-placed in Singapore to make the most of the collective wisdom of our seniors, but we must also be prepared for the challenges of an ageing society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will be a significant increase in healthcare and social expenditure, placing greater demands on families and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Also, our resident workforce will shrink, tightening our labour market and slowing economic growth further, unless we remain dynamic in our outlook, are increasingly productive in the way we work, and supplement our workforce with a calibrated inflow of workers from abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to an ageing population, there are other forces that can strain our social fabric.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to keep a close watch on income inequality and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want growth to uplift all Singaporeans and deepen our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why we will continue to invest in education and skills upgrading, to give every Singaporean the best chance to realise his or her potential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also promote sports, arts and heritage, and volunteerism and philanthropy, to build common interests and shared activities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These three shifts will not operate in isolation but interact together to affect us in profound ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of these interactions will bring new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, technology will help our older workers to stay productive and assist our caregivers to care for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With many Asian consumers at the frontier of technology adoption, there are also many opportunities for companies to meet the demands of these tech-savvy consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But these shifts can also bring new challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rapid pace of technological change may lead to older workers feeling marginalised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In some advanced economies, there is rising discontent over globalisation and technological disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as technology becomes more pervasive, the risk of cyberattacks and online radicalisation will also increase.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is in a good position to guard against such challenges and capture the opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Geographically, we are well-connected to the world, with flights to over 400 cities and shipping routes to over 600 ports globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Within Asia, we have extensive connectivity to over 100 Asian cities by air and more than 250 Asian ports by sea.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digitally, we are connected to the world with over 500 terabits per second of potential capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we will continue to enhance our connectivity by investing in digital infrastructure, as well as land links, such as the Kuala Lumpur (KL)-Singapore High Speed Rail.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an economy, we are open and free, with strong trade links and free trade agreements with many economies in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a society, we are multiracial with an international outlook, enabling us to operate in the culturally-diverse Asian and global environments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And our people are also well-educated and tech-savvy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2018 will build on this strong position.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will develop a more vibrant and innovative economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must anchor Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, welcome investments, talent and ideas to Singapore, and be bold in venturing out into new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do this, we must make innovation pervasive in our economy, develop deep capabilities in our firms and workers, and establish strong partnerships locally and abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The shifts in the global economy and the emergence of new technologies are to our advantage, because they allow us to seize opportunities beyond our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will build a smart, green and liveable city.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should take full advantage of the latest technology to improve Singaporeans’ quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is what our Smart Nation movement seeks to achieve.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve our liveability as a city, we must also enhance our urban sustainability and enable our economy to be more carbon-efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will continue to foster a caring and cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to strengthen our social safety nets and supports, especially in the face of demographic challenges like ageing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must also remain a society where all of us – as individuals, members of families, and citizens – take pride in caring for ourselves, our children and seniors, and one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Preparing for the longer-term shifts will require more resources to take care of our families, keep our people safe, invest in capabilities and develop new infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must do this amidst a period of greater geopolitical uncertainty and increasing tax competition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is, therefore, our duty and responsibility to plan ahead and ensure that we have enough resources to do all that we need to do.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must support our firms and workers to overcome near-term challenges, as well as prepare them to capture future opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will address each of these in turn.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Though our economy picked up last year, some firms remain concerned about business costs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A key driver of this is wage growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To sustain wage growth and keep business costs manageable, our firms must continue to improve productivity and achieve quality growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will support our firms to cope with near-term cost pressures by extending two measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This scheme co-funds wage increases for Singaporean employees, up to a gross monthly wage of $4,000.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, I will enhance and extend the Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also extend the CIT rebate to YA2019, at a rate of 20% of tax payable, capped at $10,000.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhancement and extension will benefit all tax-paying companies, especially smaller ones.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These changes are projected to cost an additional $475 million over the next two years  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the Marine Shipyard and Process sectors that still face weakness, I will defer the earlier-announced increases in Foreign Worker Levy rates for another year  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also strengthen support for our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been supporting those facing career transitions to stay employed and employable through the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Manpower will elaborate on this and other measures at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To capture future opportunities, our economy must transform in response to the three major shifts I mentioned earlier – the shift in global economic weight to Asia, the emergence of new technologies, and our demographic transition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And what changes do we have to make?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New technologies mean that the ways in which companies do business, create value and organise themselves will change, and change quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our companies must keep up, and our workers must adapt as the nature of jobs and the skills required evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Asia's growth means new markets, with new needs to be met.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Changing global patterns of production and consumption, together with new technologies, will bring new opportunities, but also greater competition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our businesses and workers must differentiate themselves and continue to venture abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And with an ageing population, we need to find ways to reduce manpower demand, while enabling our older workers to continue contributing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have made a good start through the ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the next phase of our ITM journey, we will take a more cluster-based approach to reap synergies and strengthen linkages across multiple industries and explore new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must strengthen the three key enablers that lay the foundation for all the ITMs – innovation, capabilities and partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we must foster pervasive innovation throughout our economy, so that we can make the best use of technology, adapt quickly, and create new value to differentiate ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we must build deep capabilities in our firms and our people, so that we can compete not on costs, but on the value and skills we bring.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we must forge strong partnerships both locally and abroad, so that our firms and people can work together to address common challenges and access new opportunities in our region and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By strengthening these three enablers, we can anchor Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the rapid pace of change and greater competition, we must make innovation pervasive throughout our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in every sector and of every size need to embrace innovation and make the best use of new technologies as a competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Take Pan-United, a local concrete and cement company.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has invested significantly in research and development (R&D), innovating new products to meet customer needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, it has developed a new type of flexible concrete that can cushion the landing impact of aircraft, reducing wear and tear of airport runways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This concrete complies with the latest specifications set by the US Federal Aviation Administration.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Pan-United also has a range of concrete varieties catering to different specifications, including one that shields against proton radiation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such product innovations have helped Pan-United expand into regional and global markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Pan-United, you might say, is a concrete example of how innovation can help a firm cement its position as a market leader.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget, we will support more firms to innovate across the entire value chain, whether they buy new solutions, build their own, or partner others to co-innovate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industry partners, like the Singapore International Chamber of Commerce and the Big Four accounting firms, have given us useful suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have studied and will implement some of them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, I will raise the tax deduction on licensing payments for the commercial use of intellectual property (IP).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This cap ensures that smaller businesses will benefit more from this measure	 .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, to support businesses to build their own innovations, I will raise the tax deduction for IP registration fees from 100% to 200%, to help firms protect their intangible assets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a virtual crowdsourcing platform, where companies can list specific challenges that can be addressed by digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will then be matched with info-communications and technology (ICT) firms and research institutes, to co-develop solutions	 .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides supporting our firms to innovate, we will do more to harness our national research capabilities to enhance our economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have built a strong research and knowledge base in our universities and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) institutes, which provides a solid foundation for an innovative economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To maintain this competitive edge, we have sustained our public sector R&D spending at 1% of GDP annually.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This new investment venture will bring together Temasek’s global investment networks and NRF’s connections with the Singapore R&D community, to grow companies that draw on IP from publicly-funded research.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also continue to harness our R&D resources to drive greater adoption of digital technologies, automation and robotics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through these programmes, our airport and seaport will become platforms for companies to develop, test and use new technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve our labour productivity, we will also expand the National Robotics Programme (NRP), to encourage wider use of robotics in the built environment sector, particularly in construction  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, capabilities to internationalise, digitalise and be more productive will be critical.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our firms, we will provide more targeted support to help them build capabilities to meet their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Broad-based measures, such as the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme have been useful in kickstarting a wider movement to improve productivity and to innovate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened that many firms have embarked on this journey.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will now build on this base and take a more targeted approach to help firms deepen the capabilities they need to continue growing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In April, we will merge the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) and International Enterprise (IE) Singapore into Enterprise Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore will provide integrated support to companies, for internationalisation as well as the development of other capabilities, so as to help them compete better both locally and abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will combine IE’s Global Company Partnership grant with SPRING's Capability Development Grant, to form an integrated Enterprise Development Grant (EDG).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: EDG will provide up to 70% co-funding for companies to develop a range of capabilities  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further support firms to internationalise, I will enhance the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDi).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will raise the amount of expenses that can qualify for DTDi without prior approval, from $100,000 to $150,000 per year of assessment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we strengthen support for firms to build capabilities, I will make adjustments to two broad-based tax schemes – the Start-up Tax Exemption and the Partial Tax Exemption.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These schemes help lower costs for smaller firms and startups, but do not directly help firms develop capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, every profitable company should pay some taxes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, starting in YA2020, I will make two changes to the schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will restrict the tax exemptions under both schemes to the first $200,000 of chargeable income.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, for startups, I will exempt 75%, instead of 100% currently, of their first $100,000 of chargeable income from corporate tax  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even with these adjustments, corporate tax will remain low for startups and smaller firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For a taxable income of $100,000, the effective corporate tax rate is 4.3% for startups and 8.1% for older firms, as compared to the headline rate of 17%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, companies, including startups and smaller firms, can tap on a wide range of Government support measures to build capabilities and grow their businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As digital technologies transform our economy, all firms must develop digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since we launched the small and medium enterprises (SMEs) Go Digital Programme last year to support companies to digitalise, more than 650 SMEs have benefited.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we are studying, with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and other industry partners, the development of a nationwide e-invoicing framework.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This can help companies improve productivity and enhance cash flow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides our firms, we must train our people in digital skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industry partners, like the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (ASME), have brought this up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since we launched the Tech Skills Accelerator (TeSA) in 2016, over 27,000 training places have been taken up or committed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Alvin is one of those who took up the training.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Retrenched after 17 years as a systems engineer, he took up TeSA's programme for cybersecurity, which equipped him with the skills needed to join ST Electronics as a white hat hacker, that is, someone who tests ICT systems for security loopholes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand TeSA into new sectors like manufacturing and professional services where digital technologies are increasingly important.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Communications and Information will speak more about this at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides digital capabilities, we must also build deep skills for workers of all ages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There must be depth in whatever we do, because this gives us the foundation to innovate and the ability to compete.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industry partners have a big role to play here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, the capabilities of a firm depend on the capabilities of its people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I recently visited Infineon, a semi-conductor manufacturer, which takes training very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Infineon plans its employee training and technology adoption in parallel, so that employees acquire relevant skills and new technologies are used effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Infineon upgraded its production processes, it also redesigned her job and trained her to use new machines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I spoke to Mdm Esah, she told me cheerfully, "I'm happy, I’m confident, I can do new things." Mdm Esah’s example shows that enterprise capabilities and human capital must be developed in tandem and be integrated with a company’s overall growth strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to work with industry partners to help the whole spectrum of our workforce develop deep skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help our people to stay relevant and develop the cross-cultural skills needed to capture opportunities in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the young, we have schemes like the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme, a work-learn programme, as well as the Go Southeast Asia Award, which matches undergraduates with regional internships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those with more work experience, we have schemes like the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy and the PCPs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, the PCP for Southeast Asia Ready Talent will equip Singaporeans with the know-how to do well regionally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our corporate leaders, it is important that they have the skills needed to drive the transformation of their businesses and industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To develop the next generation of corporate leaders, we have the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am also happy to hear that SBF and the Singapore Management University (SMU) will pilot the SBF-SMU Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD)-CHARGE Initiative this year, to help SME leaders transform their organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our older workers, we have raised the re-employment age to 67, extended the Special Employment Credit and enhanced WorkPro.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to encourage age-friendly workplaces and review how we can better support our older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we develop our people’s capabilities, we may find that skillsets in certain important fields are lacking.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To plug these gaps quickly, we are piloting the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP), to support the transfer of skills from foreign specialists to Singaporean trainers and trainees.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Manpower will elaborate at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third key enabler is to forge strong partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Competition is not the only driving force in our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Where synergies exist, we can achieve more when we work together and draw on one another’s strengths to address common challenges and capture bigger and better opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Ascendas-Singbridge, along with IE Singapore, brought together a group of Singaporean SMEs specialising in Industry 4.0 technology solutions, to set up the Singapore Manufacturing Innovation Centre in Guangzhou, China.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Centre provides these SMEs with a platform to co-create advanced manufacturing solutions with prospective Chinese clients, allowing the SMEs to reach out to the large Chinese market.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to encourage our companies to form strong partnerships, both locally and abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under PACT, companies can receive up to 70% co-funding for projects undertaken in partnership with others  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also strengthen our partnerships with overseas counterparts and anchor Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This way, our firms and people can remain plugged into the latest developments all over the world and create new ideas by interacting with people from diverse backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industry partners, like the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, have pointed out that as our region grows, there will be important needs to address in infrastructure, healthcare and other areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to develop a good understanding of these needs, so that we can innovate meaningful solutions to contribute to our region’s development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why we launched the Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) last year, for Singaporeans to gain experience and build networks overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our universities have expanded overseas internship programmes to eight new locations, including ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also launched GIA Beijing and established BLOCK71 in Suzhou and Jakarta.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides venturing abroad, we will also bring global innovation to Singapore through initiatives like the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As ASEAN Chairman this year, we hope to make a meaningful contribution by developing an ASEAN Innovation Network.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope this will strengthen the linkages among the innovation ecosystems in the region, and spark new collaborations and solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) will speak more about our ASEAN plans at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, as Asia’s growth will raise infrastructure demand, we seek to forge stronger partnerships in infrastructure development and enhance connectivity in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: China’s Belt and Road Initiative, Japan and India’s Asia-Africa Growth Corridor, and the World Bank's Infrastructure and Urban Development Hub in Singapore are just some examples of efforts to promote infrastructure development in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Office will enable infrastructure players to better tap on opportunities in the region while supporting Asia's infrastructure development and economic growth  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) and the Senior Minister of State for Law and Finance will give more details at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our TACs play an important leadership role in forging partnerships and driving industry-level advancements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through close interactions with their members, TACs understand their industries’ challenges and opportunities better than the Government can.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have seen various examples of TAC leadership and partnerships, which have helped their members uplift capabilities and overcome resource constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The TA Hub, along with the Trade Association Committee that SCCCI also set up, will encourage TACs to collaborate with and support one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In logistics, four TACs, along with SPRING and the Centre of Innovation for Supply Chain Management at Republic Polytechnic, have come together to form the Logistics Alliance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to support such efforts, through the LEAD programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I look forward to even more TACs and businesses coming on board.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The specific challenges and opportunities will differ from industry to industry, which is why we have taken a sectoral approach for the ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the key enablers in every industry and ITM are the same – innovation, capabilities and partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By fostering pervasive innovation throughout our economy, building deep capabilities in our firms and people, and forging strong partnerships locally and abroad, we can succeed in our economic transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can create and sustain a more vibrant and innovative economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a means to build a better home and provide a better quality of life for all our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will, therefore, continue to improve our living environment and make Singapore a smart, green and liveable city.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew once said, "a blighted urban jungle of concrete destroys the human spirit".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, our urban planners recognised early on that with limited land, we had to build our city with foresight, so we could provide a high-quality living environment even in a dense urban landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We designed our Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates with common spaces, parks and playgrounds, so that everyone has easy access to amenities and public spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We planted thousands of trees and toiled to transform Singapore into a Garden City and now a City in a Garden.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We may be highly urbanised, but we are not a concrete jungle.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than 40% of our island remains covered in greenery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also enacted laws against pollution and cleaned up the Singapore River.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Along the way, we became innovators in water treatment and waste management.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, Singaporeans enjoy the comforts of a modern city, along with clean air, clean water and verdant spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reputation as a clean and green city is a source of pride for Singaporeans and attracts tourists and investment to our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to improve our city and our environment and make Singapore an even better home to live, work and play in.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: History has shown that the most enduring cities are those that are adaptable, flexible and innovative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke earlier about the emergence of new technologies as a major shift.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Smart Nation movement aims to make the best use of these new technologies to improve our city, uplift our quality of life, enhance our economic competitiveness and promote social inclusion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This transformation will require a national effort by the Government, together with the private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is embarking on several strategic national projects to lay the foundation for a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are building a Smart Nation Sensor Platform to deploy sensors and "Internet of Things" devices to enhance municipal service delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are developing a National Digital Identity system to enable citizens to authenticate their identities securely and easily when making online transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also increasing the adoption of e-payments island-wide, to allow everyone to make simple, swift and seamless payments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we are opening up digital platforms for the private sector to build innovative services and will share more data with the public to facilitate co-creation  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister-in-charge of the Smart Nation initiative will elaborate more at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides building a Smart Nation, we are also collaborating with academics and corporates in research and innovation, to take Singapore’s sustainable development story to the next level.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of the strategic domains in our Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 plan is Urban Solutions and Sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we launched the Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme to drive innovation in urban development, such as ways to improve the sustainability, maintainability and reliability of buildings, raise construction productivity and create new spaces that we can live in.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also started the Closing the Waste Loop project, to use technology to minimise the environmental impact of the waste we generate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will embark on Energy Grid 2.0, to develop next-generation grid architectures that can respond quickly and reliably to changes in energy demand and supply.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve our living environment, we must also address one of the most pressing challenges the world faces – climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Climate change is more than just record-breaking temperatures, dry weather or more intense rain.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a low-lying island, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to rising sea levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why the Government has invested significantly to improve our infrastructure, including protecting our coasts and critical assets, building a weather-resilient water supply and redesigning our flood management system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must play our part to address the underlying cause of climate change to make Singapore a more liveable and sustainable city, and as a responsible member of the international community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have made various efforts to manage our greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Energy Conservation Act was enhanced last year to improve the energy efficiency of our industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are investing in public transport to make Singapore car-lite, and green-certified buildings have become a hallmark of our urban landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our early measures to be a green city have shown results.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore produces less carbon emissions per dollar of GDP than most countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We intend to further reduce our emissions intensity to make a bigger effort to combat climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will be levied on the total emissions of each of these facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first payment will be in 2020, based on emissions in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In doing so, we will take into account international climate change developments, the progress of our emissions mitigation efforts and our economic competitiveness   The carbon tax will apply uniformly to all sectors, without exemption.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the economically efficient way to maintain a transparent, fair and consistent carbon price across the economy to incentivise emissions reduction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means our initial carbon tax rate of $5 cannot be directly compared with that in other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jurisdictions with higher headline carbon prices often also have significant exemptions for particular sectors, which lowers their effective carbon prices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The carbon tax will be levied on major emitters, which account for about 80% of Singapore’s emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The remaining 20% is contributed by many other sources of varying sizes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will study how to account for these emissions and take action where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For petrol, diesel and compressed natural gas (CNG), we have excise duties, which already encourage reduction of the use of these fuels and, therefore, reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, I will not levy an additional carbon tax on petrol, diesel and CNG.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also not increase their excise duties at this point in time, but we will continue to review and adjust them periodically.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The carbon tax will encourage businesses to take measures to reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies that do so will be more competitive, as more countries impose tighter limits on their carbon emissions, and international agreements on climate change like the Paris Agreement take effect.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will also be new opportunities in areas like sustainable energy and clean technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have to start preparing early so that industries have more time to adapt.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The support for companies will be done through schemes like the Productivity Grant (Energy Efficiency) and the Energy Efficiency Fund  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More support will go to projects that achieve greater emissions abatement, beyond the basic enhancements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MTI and MEWR will share more details at a later date.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The increase in U-Save will cover the expected average increase in electricity and gas expenses for HDB households arising from the carbon tax  .

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MEWR will also work with the community to help households save energy and will announce more details at a later date.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have designated 2018 as the Year of Climate Action to encourage all Singaporeans to fight climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will speak more on our other plans to reduce energy use and carbon emissions at COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, measures like the carbon tax, along with our R&D programmes and Smart Nation investments, are to make Singapore a more liveable and sustainable city.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this effort, everyone has a role to play.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to see various community efforts in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, the Community in Bloom movement has brought together 36,000 gardening enthusiasts to cultivate more than 1,300 gardens all over Singapore, beautifying our landscape and fostering community spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And the Kayak Waterway Clean-Up Programme, run by the non-profit Waterways Watch Society, brings volunteers together to remove debris from our rivers and reservoirs while raising environmental awareness.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In ways big and small, we can all contribute to building a smarter, greener and more liveable city for all Singaporeans to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair in 15 minutes at 4.35 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.22 pm until 4.35 pm.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What ultimately matters is having a united people with a common purpose – to build the kind of society we want to live in and pass on to our children to improve.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When I first entered politics, one of my first projects was Our Singapore Conversation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It gave me and my colleagues a unique opportunity to converse with Singaporeans about their aspirations for themselves and for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: One of the things that struck me was the deep sense of responsibility that Singaporeans felt and shared – a responsibility towards the future of their family, community and country.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As Singapore undergoes demographic and societal changes that place greater demands on families, the community and the Government, we must face these changes together and respond collectively as one.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government will continue to strengthen social safety nets for those in need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, individuals, families and the community play an important role in looking out for and supporting one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is why we launched the SG Cares movement: to bring together the public, private and people sectors; create greater collective impact; and build a more caring and cohesive society for ourselves and future generations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Budget 2018 will build on the SG Cares movement in three ways.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: First, we will support individuals and families to better prepare for the future and care for one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Second, we will strengthen partnerships between the Government and the community to support our seniors and those in need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And third, we will encourage a spirit of giving in our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will first talk about how we will better support Singaporeans and their families.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Education helps our children realise their full potential.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We invest heavily in every child, to ensure that everyone, regardless of background, has access to a quality education.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget, we will increase support for education in three ways.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Second, we will update the income eligibility criteria for the Edusave Merit Bursary and the Independent School Bursary, to benefit more students from lower- to middle-income families	 .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also cover more meals for secondary school students under the School Meals Programme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Students in special education schools will also benefit from these enhancements.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Education (Schools) will provide more details at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Besides education, we will support our people to prepare for their financial needs at key stages of their lives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This starts from giving our youths a good foundation in financial literacy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will pilot a new financial education curriculum at our polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education (ITE).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also enhance existing services to Singaporeans at HDB when they buy a flat, and at Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board when they approach retirement, to enable them to make better informed decisions at these major milestones.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will support Singaporeans to prepare for their healthcare needs in old age.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are reviewing ElderShield, an insurance scheme that helps those with severe disabilities cope with the financial demands of their daily care.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To ensure that the enhanced scheme remains affordable, we will provide premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will provide an update later in the year, after the ElderShield Review Committee delivers its final recommendations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget, we will also strengthen support for family members to live with or near one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will enhance the Proximity Housing Grant (PHG).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Those buying a resale flat near their parents or children will continue to receive a PHG of $20,000.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Second, we will enhance the PHG for singles, who are often a key source of caregiving support within their families.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singles who buy a resale flat to live with their parents will now receive an enhanced PHG of $15,000.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Those who buy a resale flat near their parents will also now receive a PHG of $10,000.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Third, we will simplify the criterion for determining what is "near".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Currently, it is defined as living in the same town or within two kilometres (km).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To give applicants more choices when choosing a resale flat to live near their loved ones, including flats in nearby towns, we will revise this criterion to simply "within four km".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These enhancements will take immediate effect and cost an additional $80 million per year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together with the recently-enhanced CPF Housing Grant and the Additional CPF Housing Grant, a first-timer applicant can now receive up to $120,000 in housing grants when buying a resale flat to live with their parents, a 50% increase compared to three years ago.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also support households with their expenses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Last year, eligible HDB households received 1.5 to 3.5 months of rebate on their Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the past 10 years, the number of FDWs in Singapore has increased by about 40%, to 240,000 in 2017.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must ensure that FDW demand is commensurate with need and avoid an over-dependency on FDWs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, we recognise that some families may need help caring for young children, the elderly or family members with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, such families enjoy a monthly concessionary FDW levy of $60.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: About 80% of Singaporean FDW employers benefit from this concession.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will retain this monthly concessionary levy rate of $60.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All households with persons aged 65 and 66, which are enjoying or have enjoyed the levy concession under the aged person scheme before 1 April 2019, will continue to pay the monthly levy rate of $60.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For employers who do not qualify for the levy concession or employ multiple FDWs, we will raise the FDW levy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These changes will take effect from 1 April 2019, to give employers time to adjust.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help meet demand for part-time household services, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) is also piloting the Household Services Scheme	 .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I just spoke about how the Government will support our people to prepare for their future and care for one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our community partners play an important role in this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Being on the ground, they are more attuned to the specific needs of local communities and can respond more nimbly and quickly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, the efforts of the Government and our community partners need to be well coordinated.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our "many helping hands" need to work "hand-in-hand".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2016, I announced the pilot of the Community Networks for Seniors (CNS).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: CNS brings together Government agencies and community partners to do ABC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A is for Active Ageing, to encourage seniors to remain active and stay healthy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: B is for Befriending, to link up lonely seniors with new friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And C is for Care, for frail and vulnerable seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: CNS has helped many seniors, including Mr Willie Fox and Mrs Lena Fox.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr and Mrs Fox, who are in their 80s, told our Pioneer Generation (PG) Ambassadors that Mr Fox tired easily and had to use a wheelchair frequently.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our PG Ambassadors referred them to CNS, which enrolled them in the Care Line, a 24-hour tele-befriending service launched by the Eastern Health Alliance.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: CNS also referred Mr Fox to the Evergreen Circle Senior Activity Centre, where he now participates in weekly exercises and enjoys healthy soups cooked by volunteers!

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Fox now feels stronger and healthier and has almost stopped relying on his wheelchair.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: He and Mrs Fox are also enjoying making new friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I believe that the CNS model can meaningfully improve the lives of many other seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The CNS pilot also showed us how we can streamline and improve the delivery of services to our seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Social and healthcare needs are closely inter-related and both have an impact on the well-being of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To enable these services to be planned and delivered holistically, we will consolidate social- and health-related services for seniors under the Ministry of Health (MOH).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: From 1 April this year, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) will transfer its social aged care functions under the Senior Cluster Network and other programmes to MOH.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With this transfer, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will be designated the central implementation agency to coordinate such services for seniors and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In addition, to support the expansion of CNS nationwide, we will merge the Pioneer Generation Office (PGO) with AIC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: PGO will serve as AIC’s outreach arm in implementing CNS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It will reach out not only to Pioneers, but to all seniors aged 65 and above.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To reflect its enhanced role, PGO will be renamed “Silver Generation Office”.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our friendly Ambassadors will continue to knock on doors wearing their familiar shirts, only they will now be called the Silver Generation or SG Ambassadors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am certain seniors will continue to welcome them warmly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget, I will also top up two funds that support our seniors to age confidently in the community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since 2011, the CST has matched around $500 million in donations raised by more than 80 VWOs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To support more programmes, we will also expand CST to match donations raised for active ageing programmes	 .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Second, I will provide a $100 million top-up to the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), which provides subsidies for assistive devices and consumables for seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Another $150 million will be spent over the next five years for transport to subsidised eldercare and dialysis centres.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will review SMF in the coming years, to ensure that subsidies remain targeted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Besides improving support for our seniors, we will also improve the delivery of social services to other groups in society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our SSOs will work with these partners to harness and optimise community resources and identify areas where volunteers can complement service delivery.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our SSOs will also improve work processes and the sharing of information among organisations for better coordination.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These efforts will bring quicker and more effective assistance to our citizens, to help them get back on their feet.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will elaborate at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even as we strengthen support for our seniors and vulnerable, at the core of a caring and cohesive society are people who have the heart to give back to the community and make a difference to the lives of others.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She also volunteers as a befriender with Fei Yue Community Services.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many of her neighbours look forward to the delicious home-cooked food she brings to the Cosy Corner at her HDB block.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the process of helping others, Mdm Patma has found a stronger sense of fulfilment and purpose in life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also enhance our one-stop platform, Giving.sg, to better match donors and volunteers with charities that need support  .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In addition, I will increase support to our five Community Development Councils (CDCs).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, the Government matches $3 for every $1 that the CDCs raise, up to an annual cap of $24 million.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, we will encourage corporates to support their staff to volunteer or donate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2016, we piloted the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme (BIPS).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Businesses that support their staff to volunteer and provide services to IPCs receive a 250% tax deduction on associated costs incurred.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: An example of an IPC that has benefited is the Shared Services for Charities (SSC).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, through SSC, accounting firms provide pro bono services, such as reviews of internal controls, risk assessment and audits, to charities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These firms receive tax deductions while enabling their staff to volunteer meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will extend BIPS for another three more years, until 31 December 2021  .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Corporates can also support their staff to donate regularly to the Community Chest through SHARE.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since we launched SHARE as One at Budget 2016, which provides dollar-for-dollar matching on donations to SHARE, more than 440 new companies have come on board.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To encourage more companies to support SHARE, I will extend the SHARE as One scheme until FY2021  .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will support the ELF’s work to fund programmes in skills upgrading and employment for the most vulnerable in society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In total, we will set aside around $190 million per year to support these enhancements to encourage philanthropy and volunteerism  .

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is this shared responsibility – with individuals, families, community and the Government all playing their part and supporting one another – that has made our society what it is today and that will keep our society thriving in the years ahead.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget will support all of us to stay true to this SG Cares spirit and to work together to build a caring and cohesive society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is why I stated at the outset that our Budget is a strategic and integrated plan, taking a longer-term view, and setting out our strategic challenges clearly and plainly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This way, we can ensure a fiscally sustainable and secure future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For this decade, from 2011 to 2020, we are on a sound fiscal footing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is because we planned ahead early and made the necessary moves well before the decade began.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We raised GST from 5% to 7% as early as 2007 and introduced the Net Investment Returns (NIR) framework in 2008.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These changes allowed us to enhance our healthcare, transport and social support systems, in the first half of the decade, from 2011 to 2015.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: During this period, we introduced MediShield Life and the Pioneer Generation Package, and enhanced Workfare.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2015, we made further revenue moves to include Temasek in the NIR framework and raised personal income tax rates for the top income brackets.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These changes enabled us to sustain our spending for the second half of the decade, from 2016 to 2020.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All in all, we were able to fund a significant increase in overall Government expenditures from $55 billion in FY2011 to an estimated $89.1 billion in FY2018.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the Government has stated before, we have ensured that we have sufficient resources to meet our spending needs till 2020.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is a result of careful and prudent planning.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But in the next decade, between 2021 and 2030, if we do not take measures early, we will not have enough revenues to meet our growing needs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We expect our spending needs to continue growing across all sectors, with some rising faster and more than others.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: One of the key areas of expenditure growth will be healthcare.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This increase went into building and operating more hospitals and other healthcare facilities and enhancing healthcare subsidies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the coming decade, with an ageing population and an increasing chronic disease burden, the demands on families and the Government will rise.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will need to spend even more on healthcare.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, the average annual Government healthcare subsidies received by an elderly person is more than six times that of a younger person, or about $4,500 more.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will have to build new healthcare capacity to meet the rising demand and also invest in new medical technologies to improve care quality.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is an increase of nearly 0.8 percentage point of GDP, or about $3.6 billion in today's dollars.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Within the next decade, healthcare spending is expected to overtake education.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government will do its part to spend wisely and ensure greater value-for-money in our healthcare spending.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Everyone has a role to play, too, by taking care of our health and saving up for our own and our families’ healthcare needs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Another key area of expenditure increase will be infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have increased our infrastructure spending8 from $8.5 billion in FY2011 to an estimated $20 billion in FY2018.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are building and upgrading flats, expanding and maintaining our rail and bus networks, and keeping public transport fares low for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the next five years, the annual subsidies for keeping our buses and trains running will be comparable to the amount we spend on pre-employment training in polytechnics and ITEs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And this does not even include the cost of building public transport infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the next decade, we will need to spend more to develop new infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will expand our rail network by over 100 km, redevelop different parts of Singapore like the Jurong Lake District, Punggol Digital District and Woodlands North Coast, and rejuvenate our ageing infrastructure, such as water pipes and HDB flats and lifts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also build Changi Airport Terminal 5 (Changi T5), Tuas Port and the KL-Singapore High Speed Rail so as to ready ourselves for long-term economic trends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These are massive investments to anchor Singapore as the centre for economic activity in the region, create jobs, enhance liveability and serve as a foundation for future growth.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As my colleague, the Minister for National Development has said, "We are not done building Singapore yet." Third, we will also have to invest more in security to keep Singapore safe.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The terrorism threat to Singapore is at its highest in recent years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The range of threats we face is also wider, from major cyberattacks to online self-radicalisation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To counter these threats, we will need to: enhance the operational readiness of our officers; leverage technologies to enhance our response; and partner the community, so that we are all well-equipped to respond in emergencies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Besides healthcare, infrastructure and security, we will also have to sustain our investments in education to give our young a good start.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even though our student cohorts are falling, we are spending more per child and dedicating more resources to help everyone reach his or her potential.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In FY2018, our education spending9 is estimated at $12.8 billion.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are investing more in preschool education to give every child a good foundation from a younger age.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will continue to invest in lifelong learning to help Singaporeans reskill and upskill so that they can access good jobs and thrive in the new economy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Hence, there is a need to strengthen our fiscal footing to meet these growing expenditure needs and to prepare for any unforeseen ones.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have already spoken about this at last year's Budget and said that we would study various options.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Prime Minister also mentioned this in November last year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our fundamental strategy is to grow our economy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With a strong economy, we will have more resources with which we can meet the needs and aspirations of our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The work of the FEC and the strategies I laid out earlier are, therefore, critical.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, we must continue to manage our expenditure growth carefully and get the best value for every dollar we spend.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At 19% of GDP, our estimated overall Government expenditure10 in FY2018 is leaner than most developed economies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And we have been able to get good value for our money, delivering good outcomes in areas like healthcare and education, which are highly ranked internationally.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even so, to emphasise the need to be more prudent, I announced a permanent 2% downward adjustment to the budget caps of Ministries and Organs of State last year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This year, I will further moderate the pace of Ministries’ budget growth.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our agencies are also on the lookout for ways to be more efficient and effective.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: My earlier announcement to merge PGO with AIC and make AIC the central implementation agency for seniors is one example.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Another is the Land Transport Authority (LTA), which has designed a four-in-one facility, integrating one bus and three rail depots in a single development.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This achieved significant cost savings and freed up about 44 hectares of land.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is larger than our Singapore Zoo and River Safari put together!

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Other agencies are tapping on emerging technologies to improve productivity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: JTC Corporation, for instance, has co-developed a robot with the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) to facilitate building inspection works, reducing manpower and time required by 50%.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For our infrastructure investments, the key challenge is that certain expenditures can be very lumpy, with hefty upfront investments.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Yet, the benefits are enjoyed many years down the road.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To address this challenge, we will do two things.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: First, where possible, we will save ahead in preparation for these lumpy investments.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will help reduce the burden in future years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2015, we set up the Changi Airport Development Fund to start saving for Changi T5.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This can be topped up in future years when our fiscal position allows.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Second, we are looking at borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies which build infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will help spread the cost of certain larger investments over more years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These infrastructure projects, once completed, will generate economic returns over many years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The borrowing arrangements for these projects will, hence, help distribute the share of funding more equitably across generations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For example, the National Environment Agency (NEA) will look at borrowing to finance the upcoming Integrated Waste Management Facility.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: LTA will also look at borrowing for upcoming projects, such as the KL-Singapore High Speed Rail and the Johor Bahru (JB)-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Changi Airport Group, too, will look at borrowing for Changi T5.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Besides spreading out the costs to better match when the benefits of the investments accrue, such long-term borrowings will also help to develop our bond market.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help lower the financing cost, the Government will consider providing guarantees for some of these long-term borrowings for critical national infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A Government guarantee will enhance the confidence of creditors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is another way to use the strength of our Reserves to back our infrastructure projects, without directly drawing on the Reserves.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
